rows.title: Lamont’s plan to close $2B deficit could be to tap CT’s $3B rainy day fund
rows.standfirst: Don’t expect to see Gov. Ned Lamont propose big tax hikes or huge spending cuts to close a $2B deficit.

rows.title: Lamont leans on reserves to cover deficit, says lawmakers don’t need to act until January
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont recommends tapping 60% of the record-setting budget reserve to cover most of a $2 billion budget deficit.

rows.title: Surging tax receipts take a huge chunk out of state’s projected budget deficit
rows.standfirst: The improved fiscal picture increases the likelihood Gov. Ned Lamont can avert major tax hikes next spring.

rows.title: CT economy will struggle until at least 2030 to recover from COVID, UConn report warns
rows.standfirst: The UConn think tank also said state has hurt itself by failing to make investments in information technology.

rows.title: Lawmakers eye higher ed, nonprofits for state bailout as COVID continues
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers say the state should help programs, like higher education, beset by the COVID pandemic. Will the governor agree?

rows.title: Advocates press state regulators to extend moratoriums on power utility shut-offs
rows.standfirst: With temperatures dropping, advocates for Connecticut’s vulnerable are urging state regulators to extend moratoriums on electricity and other utility shut-offs.
